parole.significato: infertile (not capable of reproducing children; not fertile)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *ahtëra (“barren, sterile”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *akšterɜ. Cognate with Finnish ahtera, Livonian ǭ’dõrz, Võro aher, Votic ahõr, Erzya якстерь (jaksteŕ).

From Proto-Finnic *etä, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *ečkä, *ečä. Cognate to Finnish etä-, Ingrian etää, edähitee (“far”), Livonian edeh (“forwards, against”), Veps edahaks (“far”), and possibly Moksha [script needed] (ičkəźä, “far”). See also esi.
From Proto-Finnic *hoi, *hui, from Proto-Finno-Permic *šoje, *šuje. Cognate to Finnish hui (“spool”)

parole.significato: to sit (to be in such a position where the buttock rests on some kind of base and the back is upright)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *istudak (“to sit”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *isɜ-. Cognate to Finnish istua, Erzya озамс (ozams).
From Proto-Finnic *jivä, variant of *jüvä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *jewä, ultimately borrowed from Proto-Indo-European *yéwos.

From Proto-Finnic *jahëda, ultimately derived from Proto-Finno-Permic *jakša, whence Erzya якшамо (jakšamo) and Moksha якшама (jakšama, “cold, frost”). This root can be seen in Proto-Finnic *jahtudak (“to cool down”) (with the suffix *-tudak (modern Estonian -tuma)), whence modern Estonian jahtuma.
From Proto-Finnic *jämedä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *jämä-. Cognates include Livonian jamdõ, Votic and Ingrian jämmiä, dialectal Finnish jämeä, Livvi jämei, Ludian dʹämed and Veps jämed.
From Proto-Finnic *korjat'ak, probably from Proto-Finno-Permic *korja-. Cognates include Finnish korjata (“to repair; to gather”), Livonian kuoŗŗõ (“to collect, pick”) and Votic kõrjõtõ (“to cover”).
Inherited from Proto-Finnic *louna, from Proto-Finno-Permic *lowna. Cognate with Finnish lounas.

parole.significato: to pay (to give money for work done, a service, goods received, etc.)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *maksadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *maksa-. Cognate with Finnish maksaa and Votic mahsa.
From Proto-Finnic *marja, from Proto-Finno-Permic *mërja. Cognate with Finnish marja, Ingrian marja, and Votic marjõ.
From Proto-Finnic *meeli, From Proto-Finno-Permic *mäle. Cognates include Finnish mieli, Votic meeli, Northern Sami miella, Moksha мяль (mäľ) and Komi-Zyrian мыл (myl).
From Proto-Finnic *oksa, from Proto-Finno-Permic *oksa.

parole.significato: to puke, to throw up, to vomit
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *oksëntadak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *okse- Cognate with Finnish oksentaa and Votic õhsõtõ.
From Proto-Finnic *orja, from Proto-Finno-Permic *orja. Cognates include Finnish orja.

parole.significato: to poke, to thrust, to stab
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *pistädäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *pistä-. Cognates include Finnish pistää, Northern Sami bastit (“to be able to”) and Eastern Mari пышташ (pyštaš). See also püsima.

From Proto-Finnic *pähkeli, from Proto-Finno-Permic *päškɜ. Cognates include Finnish pähkinä, Votic pähčene, Livonian pē’gõz, Veps pähkim, Ingrian päähkänä, Erzya пеште (pešte), Moksha пяште (päšte), Eastern Mari пӱкш (pükš), Udmurt пашпу (pašpu, “hazelnut bush”) and possibly also Komi-Zyrian пашкан

From Proto-Finnic *pisüdäk, from Proto-Finno-Permic *pise-w- with the passive suffix -w- causing labialization of the initial -i- to -ü-. Cognates include Finnish pysyä, Livonian püzüö, Ludian püzüdä, Veps püžuda, Võro püsümä, Votic püsüä, Erzya пезнамс (peznams), Moksha пезомс (pezoms) and Eastern

parole.significato: pregnant (carrying a fetus developing in its organism, expecting a child)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *rasëda (“tired; pregnant; heavy”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *ranśe. Related to raske (“heavy”) (from *raskëda, where the -k- is a derivational suffix). Replaced earlier raskejalgne (literally “having heavy feet”).

parole.significato: A prefix signifying inner, internal, interior, inward; indoor; inland.
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *sicä, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śićä. Cognate to Finnish sisä-.

From Proto-Finnic *sulkëdak, from Proto-Finno-Permic [Term?]. Cognate to Finnish sulkea, Karelian sulkie, Votic sulko (“cold, runny nose”), Erzya сёлгомс (śolgoms, “to close”) and Moksha сёлгомс (śolgoms, “to close”).
From Proto-Finnic *säski, from Proto-Finno-Permic *śäśke.

From Proto-Finnic *tahko, from Proto-Finno-Permic [Term?]. Cognate to Finnish tahko, Votic tahko (“wood block”), Udmurt тӥш (tiš, “axe eye, backside of a blade”), and Komi-Zyrian тыш (tyš, “axe eye”). The meaning of "hone" seen in the Finnic family is possibly originally from a compound word - *tahk
From Proto-Finnic *tallat'ak, possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic [Term?]. Cognate with Finnish tallata, Votic talloa, Ingrian tallata, Livvi tallata, Veps tallata and Komi-Zyrian талявны (taľavny).
From Proto-Finnic *tammi, from Proto-Finno-Permic *tamme. Cognate to Finnish tammi.

From Proto-Finnic *tohtidak, from Proto-Finno-Permic *tošte-. Possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰers-, in which case it would be distantly related to English dare. Cognate with Finnish tohtia.

parole.significato: wind (perceptible movement of air due to natural causes)
parole.testo: From Proto-Finnic *tuuli, from Proto-Finno-Permic *towle.
From Proto-Finnic *uni, from Proto-Finno-Permic *une, cognate to Finnish uni, Votic uni, Ludian uńi, and Erzya он (on, “dream”).

From Proto-Finnic *vasta, from Proto-Finno-Permic *wasta (“a place opposite or across”). Cognate to Finnish vasta, Votic vassõ, Northern Sami vuostá, Erzya вастомс (vastoms, “to meet; to receive”), Moksha васта (vasta, “place; distance”) and possibly Western Mari ваштареш (vaštareš, “against; across

parole.significato: tired (in need of some rest or sleep)
parole.testo: Past participle of väsima (“to get tired; to fatigue”), from Proto-Finnic *väsüdäk (“to tire; to fatigue”), possibly from Proto-Finno-Permic *wäśä-. Equivalent to väsima + -nud (past active participle). Cognate with Finnish väsynyt.

From Proto-Finnic *äijä (“old man”), from Proto-Finno-Permic *äjjä (“old man”). Cognates include Finnish äijä (“old man”), Votic äjje, Ingrian äijä (“grandfather; father-in-law; old man”), Karelian äijä (“a lot of”), Livvi äijy (“many, much”), Ludian äij (“a lot of”), Veps äi (“many, much”); Norther
